title: Arkret Event Envelope
description: Single canonical wire object for durable and actor-private Events. kind + schema-validated payload is the only producer-authored business fact; reducer cell targets and lattice operations are derived from the registered reducer contract and never supplied on wire. DataEvents carry seal_ref/auth_context; Control Moves carry seal_basis and optional preconditions. proof.event_digest hashes canonical producer bytes, including the complete actor_id, after removing proofs, unsigned, and the sole reducer-stamped top-level field actor_kind. Signed scope_ref is included in the digest and is independently checked against payload-derived security scope. Signal uses signal-envelope.schema.json; point-to-point device verification and secret distribution use device-message.schema.json.

kind.description: Standard ak.* Event kinds MUST appear in artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json. State convergence is defined by the registered pure reducer over kind + payload; producers do not submit cell writes.

scope_ref.description: Required producer-signed security scope. The closed union is ordinary existing realm, circle, or native sidecar scope plus the create-only realm_genesis exception. It enters proof.event_digest and E2EE AAD. Reducers independently derive the exact scope from schema-validated payload and accepted references; missing dependencies, nonexistent scope, realm_id mismatch, omitted sidecar_id, substituting circle for sidecar, or any unequal field is fail closed. Sidecar domain Event kinds remain Extension-owned; recognizing this native security shape does not make Kernel interpret the Sidecar reducer. Exact product targets remain inside recipient-visible ciphertext.

actor_id.description: Complete identity of the principal whose Realm/cell state the Event mutates and to whom the durable fact is attributed. Account variants carry their Station namespace inside actor_id; a service variant carries the directly authoring service identity. When executed_by is absent, the proof signer maps to actor_id. When executed_by is present, actor_id remains the principal of record while the actual executor and proof signer map to executed_by.

executed_by.description: Optional complete identity of the actual executor for a delegated write. This covers both an agent/applet/service acting for a controller actor and a controller acting under explicit managed-principal delegation to write an Agent principal's control state. actor_id is always the principal of record; executed_by is the principal that issued and signed the wire write. When present, MUST appear together with authorization_ref. Applet delegated writes also MUST carry applet_id. Enters canonical event bytes, event digest, and E2EE AAD. Receivers MUST verify that the proof verification method and admission evidence map to the exact executed_by variant (not actor_id) and MUST NOT synthesize an actor_id signature.

authorization_ref.description: Optional. Required when executed_by is present. Prefer a materialized ak:grant:* id; an event id is allowed only when it points to the accepted grant/delegation event that produced the effective authorization; a DID-document delegation URL (did_delegation_ref) is allowed when the delegation is expressed in the principal DID document; realm_authority_root_ref designates this Realm's registered authority-root cell. Exactly two non-grant profile sources are admitted here: direct_conversation_participant_authority_ref, paired with one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_binding Event reference, and direct_conversation_bootstrap_authority_ref, paired with one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_founding_unit Event reference for the pre-binding founding phase. An arbitrary Event/cell MUST NOT be treated as participant authority. When executed_by is present, authorization_ref binds the executor delegation instead and the DM profile source is evaluated as an independent conjunctive profile gate.

applet_id.description: Optional signed Applet provenance. Required by ak.profile.applet_* when the Event is introduced by an Applet, Ghost Actor, bridge, or delegated applet path. Enters canonical event bytes and therefore is covered by proof.event_digest. When present, authorization_ref MUST also be present and resolve to a real active registration/capability grant binding this applet_id, registration_epoch, action and resource per zh/extensions/applet-integration.md sections 4, 8 and 11. Service-actor self-signature proves provenance but is not an authorization substitute.

external_ref.description: Optional signed external provenance reference for Applet / bridge-originated Events. It is covered by event_digest and MUST NOT be carried only in unsigned when used for loop prevention, audit, or external-message idempotency. Must not contain unauthorized external plaintext.

actor_kind.description: Reducer-stamped projection of the actor_id Actor Profile's actor_kind at write time (see zh/models/event-and-patch.md and zh/models/actor.md). Lets audit/forensic/offline readers classify the event without resolving Actor Profile. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and never appears as actor_id; device actions are attributed to the owning user/organization principal DID. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (schema_violation reason=actor_kind_reducer_managed); reducer stamps it during accept. Immutable once written and excluded from producer proof.event_digest.

hlc.description: Advisory hybrid logical clock. INCLUDED in canonical bytes for signing and event digest (so it is integrity-protected and cannot be rewritten by relays), but semantically advisory: used only as a deterministic tiebreaker for timeline display when two events are causally unreachable. MUST NOT influence authorization, lattice join, Control Move precondition comparison, or Seal finality. See encoding.md §7 and event-auth-state-resolution.md §3 rule 1.

prev_refs.description: Actor-chain causal predecessors as complete Event IDs. Each Event ID carries the digest suite code and all 32 digest octets and is committed by this Event's digest preimage. For semantic refs (authorized_by, after, state_witness, inclusion_proof, ...), use refs[].

refs.description: Semantic refs with role. did_recovery_anchor is reserved exclusively for ak.device.reanchor and is enforced bidirectionally below; all other common roles remain open extension tokens.

causal_refs.description: DataEvent semantic causal predecessors by event_digest. A DataEvent carrying payload.patch MUST provide at least one causal_ref and MUST identify exactly one accepted base-head digest for every target cell; the per-cell uniqueness and post-state reconstruction checks are reducer semantics. Other DataEvents may use this field for business causality. These refs are not global completeness proofs.

preconditions.description: Control Move only. Pre-state predicates that must hold under the seal_basis governance view; if any fails, the entire event fails. DataEvents MUST NOT carry preconditions.

seal_ref.description: DataEvent only. Accepted control-plane Seal id used as the authorization basis. Receivers verify identity/key/capability validity at this seal and apply revocation freshness rules.

auth_context.description: DataEvent only. Pins the signing key id and epoch used to verify authorization at seal_ref. The signing principal is the complete executed_by when present, otherwise the complete actor_id. Effective capabilities are derived from the accepted governance basis, never selected by the producer.

seal_basis.description: Control Move only. Signed governance basis for preconditions and reducer derivation. The canonical sorted Seal leaves are the sole producer commitment; receivers resolve and verify each Seal and deterministically recompute the covered control set and joined state. Seal roots remain on the Seal itself and are not copied into the Event.

unsigned.description: Local / transport-only metadata (server-derived hints, redaction reason, age). NOT covered by signature or event digest.

proofs.description: Producer proofs sign canonical Event bytes, including the complete actor_id and executed_by when present. After local admission, the origin Station named by the account signer variant appends at most one station_admission proof that binds the exact producer proof it verified; a directly authoring service is its own service identity. proofs and unsigned remain excluded from event_digest; federation and backfill preserve the accepted Event byte-for-byte.

requirements.description: Schema, feature, and critical-extension requirements declared by this event. All sub-fields enter the canonical event bytes and the proof event_digest. Reducer selection is derived from the Realm reducer-profile control cell, never declared by an ordinary Event. Receivers MUST fail closed on any unknown critical entry.

schema.description: Schema profile ids this event depends on.

features.description: Features this event requires; receiver MUST fail closed if any is unknown.

critical_extensions.description: Critical extension declarations; each entry MUST have id, extension_scope, fail_closed=true.

allOf.$comment: Machine-closed accepted-Event producer signer-evidence rule. When an admission proof is present it owns historical producer-key validation and the producer proof omits its external evidence pair. A no-admission envelope is shared by caller submission and retained direct-history replay, so its pair requirement is enforced by the consuming operation/profile rather than inferred from this context-free schema.
A patch-bearing DataEvent is identified by its required seal_ref and payload.patch. It needs at least one causal base; exact per-target-cell matching remains a reducer check.

Signed Applet provenance invariants. external_ref is only meaningful when bound to a signed applet_id, and every Applet-originated write, including service-actor self-signature, must cite a real accepted active authorization/delegation grant.

Closed direct-conversation participant authority reference. Direct participant writes cite the registered source token and one exact critical binding Event evidence ref. Delegated Agent writes use authorization_ref for the executor delegation and satisfy participant authority independently in the profile evaluator.

Closed direct-conversation bootstrap authority reference. Pre-binding founding-phase writes cite the registered bootstrap source token and one exact critical founding-unit Event evidence ref, because no binding Event exists yet to cite.
Known active non-reducer Event kinds MUST NOT carry CBA fields: preconditions/seal_ref/auth_context/seal_basis.

Conflict-recovery event detection: any precondition with op=head_in implies conflict recovery semantics. When triggered, refs[] MUST contain BOTH a state_witness and an inclusion_proof (event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1). Schema-level enforcement; reducer-level verify re-checks.
MUST contain at least one state_witness ref
MUST contain at least one inclusion_proof ref
ak.redaction is the cross-object redaction kind. Its payload class excludes Message so that a Message can only reach state=redacted through the object-scoped ak.message.redact.
ak.device.reanchor is the only event allowed to carry did_recovery_anchor, and it must carry exactly one critical ref whose id has did:webvh versionId shape.
Count the reserved role independent of critical so one critical plus one non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

Any Event carrying did_inception is confined to the closed self-principal PCR-genesis shape and carries exactly one critical ref. A delegated Agent PCR create intentionally carries no did_inception; batch/reducer admission distinguishes self-principal genesis from delegated Agent genesis by comparing the complete actor_id, executed_by, authorization_ref, PCR binding and DID subject, which JSON Schema cannot express.
Count the reserved role independently so a critical ref plus a non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

A agent_control Realm create without did_inception is syntactically reserved for delegated managed-principal genesis. Requiring the delegation pair prevents a self-principal caller from falling through to ordinary realm.create capability admission; the delegated_pcr_genesis verifier performs the actor/DID/service/realm comparisons that JSON Schema cannot express.

An applet_managed_control PCR genesis is reachable only through one immutable Applet-managed actor provision authority Event. The admission verifier cross-binds the provision payload and initial_resolution; this shape cannot fall through to generic realm.create authority.

Reject these top-level field names. The Event Envelope root is closed (additionalProperties=false); extension data belongs in payload or requirements.critical_extensions. The root field names type / auth_refs / target_ref / operation_id are dropped and MUST NOT appear at the root; use kind / refs[role=authorized_by] / payload.* fields / SDK-internal id instead (see operations-sync.md §5).

anyOf.$comment: auth_refs is dropped; it MUST NOT appear at the root, use refs[role=authorized_by]

allOf.$comment: zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.0: ak.realm.create MUST omit realm_id and use the realm_genesis scope. Every Realm, including Collaboration, Direct Conversation, human PCR, and Agent PCR, derives realm_id = retype(event_id, "realm") from this create Event. The uniform omission leaves one receiver-derived genesis form and avoids the digest cycle. Every other kind MUST carry realm_id.

external_ref.description: Signed external provenance. Extension profiles define exact field vocabulary; common fields include protocol, network_id, instance_id, user_id, location_id, event_id, external_id, and url. Implementations MUST preserve all fields in canonical bytes and MUST NOT use unsigned.external_ref for security decisions.

canonical_event_timestamp.description: Canonical Event Envelope/proof timestamp. UTC Z form with exactly three millisecond digits; whole-second shorthand, finer fractions, and numeric offsets are forbidden.

oneOf.description: Native controller-and-owned-Agents private scope. It is not a Circle and has no editable membership.

Genesis scope for ak.realm.create only. It carries no realm_id because the receiver derives every Realm id, including Collaboration, Direct Conversation, human PCR, and Agent PCR, as retype(event_id, "realm") from this create Event (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.0). The uniform omission also prevents the digest cycle.

profile_ref.description: Profile that defines this extension's semantics when schema_ref is not the exact governing profile.

parameters.description: Closed extension-specific parameter bag. Unknown top-level fields are forbidden; extension-defined data belongs here and is interpreted only after id/schema_ref support is sealed.

material_digest.description: Optional digest of out-of-band extension material when parameters would be too large for the event envelope.

event_ref.description: Complete Event reference carrying the suite wire_code and all 32 digest octets. It is suitable for authorization, equality, deduplication, Seal coverage, and exact replay after normal recomputation and acceptance checks.

did_delegation_ref.description: DID URL of a non-device controller/organization authority entry that designates executed_by for an operation profile. Principal device authorization never uses this DID-document branch: it resolves through accepted PCR evidence. Historical DID authority is resolved at the Event accepted-at basis.

realm_authority_root_ref.description: Designates the registered authority-root cell of the envelope's own realm_id. This is a closed constant, not a general cell_ref: only the singleton ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell carries Realm owner authority, and widening it to an arbitrary cell_ref would let any projected cell be presented as an authorization source. Reducer MUST resolve it against that cell in the Event's authorization basis and verify controller_id == the authorizing principal plus the cell's authority_generation. Inside the ak.realm.create genesis batch the staged root value is used and the Event MUST descend from the same batch's create Event through prev_refs; outside that batch an accepted-Seal inclusion proof is required and a staged proof MUST be rejected. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 3.2.

direct_conversation_participant_authorit.description: The daily profile-scoped non-grant authorization source accepted by Event.authorization_ref. It is meaningful solely in ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and requires one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_binding Event reference. The evaluator rederives the pair's unique immutable binding, exact-two participant membership, Realm/Strand/MLS cross-binding, lifecycle, both directional Contact heads/scopes and action-specific gates without consulting Consent; this constant never authorizes arbitrary Realm or third-party writes.

direct_conversation_bootstrap_authority_.description: Pre-binding profile-scoped non-grant authority for a Direct Conversation between accepted founding unit and first legal binding endorsement. It requires one critical founding-unit ref. provisional_history_send authorizes only founder actions in the one scope-derived group; exact_pair_founding_completion applies once that same group holds exact authorized pair leaves. Both retire after the first binding. Neither phase authorizes a second Genesis/group, policy, grant, a third participant, another Strand or ordinary membership writes.

membership_compensation_delegation_ref.description: Content-addressed accepted-at membership compensation delegation. It is valid only for ak.member.state leave/remove submitted with the matching closed Event submission transport-only membership_compensation_evidence carrier and registered single-use evaluator. This carrier is not an ak:sidecar: Agent Sidecar object and has no participant semantics.

semantic_ref.description: Closed typed locator union. State witnesses use a SealRef plus inline typed Merkle proof; grant/event roles use the exact provenance EventId. Signer-resolution evidence is carried exactly once by each producer/station proof's required signer_resolution_evidence_ref and signer_resolution_evidence_digest, never as a SemanticRef. Unknown critical roles fail closed.

proof.description: Generic detached-JWS proof shape reused by non-Event schemas (snapshot signature, snapshot witness attestations, identity receipts, handle claims, etc.). MUST NOT be used as the shape of Event Envelope `proofs[]` — Event proofs reference $defs/event_proof and bind canonical Event bytes via `event_digest`. Non-Event signed objects MUST define an object-family signing-context constant and include it in the canonical proof binding object with payload_digest; the context constant is not a wire field in this generic shape. drift detection: `payload_digest#event_proof` in forbidden-wire-fields.json is the hard-reject mirror of this rule. New non-Event signed objects MAY $ref this shape; new signed Event-shaped objects MUST instead $ref event_proof.

kind.description: Generic detached JWS proof over a canonical non-Event payload binding object that includes an object-family context constant.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key for this non-Event detached proof. Same pattern as $defs/event_proof.verification_method; semantics are decoupled from Event proof (see $defs/event_proof for the Event-only shape).

payload_digest.description: Generic non-Event detached-proof hash. This $defs/proof shape is reused by non-Event schemas; Event.properties.proofs references $defs/event_proof and MUST use event_digest instead.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for non-Event proofs. HandleClaim core, status and revocation carriers make issuer_attestation, holder_acceptance, status_attestation and revocation_authorization load-bearing. governance_authorization marks a resource-governance-key authorization (directory withdraw/takedown-appeal, discovery-directory.md 8.7.1). Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it load-bearing.

station_admission_proof.description: Origin Station admission proof over canonical_json({context:'ak.station_admission_proof.v1',event_digest,producer_proof_digest,producer_verification_method,producer_signing_key,producer_signer_resolution_evidence_ref?,producer_signer_resolution_evidence_digest?,signer_resolution_evidence_ref,signer_resolution_evidence_digest,accepted_at,verification_method}). The optional producer pair freezes the original producer evidence root when that signer regime has portable evidence; Agent federation requires it. The unprefixed signer pair continues to bind the Station proof's own service signer evidence.

verification_method.description: Station verification method whose controller projects to the station_id inside the Event signer account ActorId. A directly authoring service proof instead projects to that service ActorId's service_id.

producer_proof_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the complete producer_event_proof object actually verified by the origin service.

producer_verification_method.description: Must equal the bound producer proof verification_method byte-for-byte.

producer_signing_key_did.description: Public signing key that verifies the exact producer proof at admission time.

producer_signer_resolution_evidence_dige.description: Must be present as a matching pair with producer_signer_resolution_evidence_ref. Agent admission requires the pair and it resolves to the exact frozen CurrentAdmission root.

signer_resolution_evidence_digest.description: Must equal the digest encoded by signer_resolution_evidence_ref and resolve to the exact Station verification method used by this proof.

kind.description: Actor, device or service signature over the registered producer-proof transcript. When the Event has no station_admission proof, signer_resolution_evidence_ref and signer_resolution_evidence_digest are required and included. When a valid admission proof exists, both fields are forbidden and that proof's producer_signing_key is the historical producer-key truth.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the Event-signing key. Generic verification extracts the canonical bare DID base under the active method adapter, validates that method history/key, projects the base DID to did_core_id, and compares it byte-for-byte with the principal component of executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise; a did_core_id is never concatenated into a DID URL. For principal device proofs the fragment MUST be the full device_id (`ak:device:<uuidv7>`), so receivers can resolve the complete actor_id plus device_id through the device directory. The sole exception is an Event whose selected admission variant is did_root_anchor: its closed verifier MUST instead require verification_method to equal an active controller-proof verification method from the one critical did_inception/did_recovery_anchor entry and verify the controller proof/update authority against that referenced did:webvh history; a root did:key controller is not rewritten to the principal actor_id. This exception cannot apply to any other Event.

signer_resolution_evidence_ref.description: Required only for the direct/DID-root/native producer regime without station_admission; forbidden otherwise.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for handle-claim proofs. Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it required.

producer_event_proof.description: Producer Event proof. The signer maps to the complete executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise. Its event_digest covers canonical producer Event bytes including that complete identity and excluding proofs, unsigned and reducer-stamped actor_kind. The event-level proof-regime validator enforces exactly one branch: a valid station_admission proof means producer signer evidence fields are absent and the admission-bound producer_signing_key verifies this proof; without such admission both signer evidence fields are present and resolve to this exact verification_method.

event_proof.description: Closed Event proof union. Callers submit producer_event_proof only; the origin Station may append one station_admission proof after successful local admission.
